newsitem.title: USA: Georgia lawmakers honor ex-Olympic bombing suspect.
newsitem.headline: Georgia lawmakers honor ex-Olympic bombing suspect.

text.p: Security guard Richard Jewell was honoured by the Georgia House of Representatives Wednesday for saving lives at the bombing at Centennial Olympic Park last summer.

A resolution passed unanimously by the House said Jewell, who federal investigators initially identified as a suspect, helped prevent more people from being killed or injured when a crude pipe bomb exploded during a rock concert on July 27.

"The tragedy would have been much, much worse" if Jewell had not discovered a suspicious knapsack containing the bomb and encouraged people to leave the area, said state representative Mitchell Kaye, a Republican from Marietta, Ga.
"He is a perfect example of how a high-profile investigation can make an innocent man infamous, completely contrary to the presumption of innocence until proven guilty," Kaye said.
The resolution was passed with no debate.

Jewell was identified as a suspect a few days after the bombing, but was cleared by federal officials in October. Authorities have not publicly identified any other suspects in the bombing, which led to two deaths and more than 100 injuries.
